attacks.claim: The QA table reports the staff pilot as complete, with 0 misdelivered texts and 2 copy fixes shipped. The Rollout section schedules that pilot for Nov 2-6, and today is 2026-10-26, so the pilot has not happened. The header also says all QA ran on staging, which conflicts with a pilot on real holds. The pass result is unsupported, and it is the only real-world evidence of correct delivery before the all-cardholder launch.
attacks.evidence: "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified" vs. "1. Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above)."

attacks.claim: The fixed announcement copy says text alerts are "for every cardholder". Juvenile cards cannot see the option, and the copy does not say it is opt-in. The wording is inaccurate and can be corrected cheaply before it is posted on posters and the newsletter.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." vs. "juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: The message template shows two holds with a single single-use code. The artifact does not say whether one code opens multiple cells or how batched holds at different locations are handled. It also does not say how patrons on email or phone fallback receive the locker code.
attacks.evidence: "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913"; "Codes are single-use"; "extra holds are batched into one message"

attacks.claim: The locker_pickup rollback remaps holds to the desk but does not say whether already-issued locker codes are revoked, or how staff open occupied cells when the locker flow is disabled.
attacks.evidence: "staff move items to the holds shelf, hold deadlines extend 3 days and patrons are notified of the new location"

attacks.claim: The opt-in confirmation text is sent to any number entered in the form, and no per-number throttle or abuse control is described. The form is behind login, which limits exposure, and the spend cap bounds the cost.
attacks.evidence: "We send a confirmation text; texts start only after the patron replies YES." ABSENT: rate limiting on the phone field
